headline: Iran mediation hopes pull WTI below $102 as Moody's relief cuts the OAT–Bund spread 13bp
summary: Qatari and Saudi-led mediation with Tehran trimmed the war premium in crude, with December WTI settling down $1.51 at $101.76 and Brent near $115, though weekend Houthi strikes on Saudi pipelines kept dips shallow and RBOB edged up to $3.2185. Softer oil eased hike fears just enough for gold to reclaim $4,000 while silver stalled near $54. Treasuries marked time before Wednesday's Fed, the 2-year a touch higher after a soft auction, while French bonds rallied hard after Moody's held France at Aa3 and Bunds slipped on a firmer Ifo.
drivers: Qatari envoys and Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials held talks in Tehran, pulling December WTI down $1.51 (-1.5%) to $101.76 and Brent about $2 to near $115. Houthi claims of strikes on East-West pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport limited the drop.
Moody's hold sparks a French relief rally

After Moody's kept France at Aa3 (negative outlook), the 10-year OAT fell about 12bp to near 4.91% and the spread to Bunds shrank about 13bp to roughly 154bp, its biggest one-day narrowing since 2020. Calmer weekend protests helped.
Fed week: hold priced, December in play

Markets price about a 90% chance the Fed holds on Wednesday but 75–80% odds of a December hike. A $69bn 2-year sale tailed slightly at 4.708%, nudging the 2-year up about 3bp to 4.71% while the 10-year held near 4.99%.
Gold back above $4,000 on cheaper oil
Spot gold rose about 0.5% to near $4,015 after Friday's $3,975 low as lower crude eased inflation worry, but hike odds kept it below $4,032 resistance. Silver was flat near $53.9.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled down $1.51 (-1.5%) at $101.76; Brent fell about $2 to near $115 from a six-month high.
oil.why: Crude gave back part of last week's surge as Qatari mediators and Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iran's leaders in Tehran, raising hopes the US–Iran conflict can be contained. Dip buying limited the loss: the Houthis claimed weekend strikes on pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Riyadh airport, and Murban's jump showed physical buyers still pay up for barrels outside Hormuz. Diesel fell 1.5% to $4.91.
oil.outlook: Bias still firm but choppier: Brent $110–120, WTI $97–106. Confirmed damage to Saudi export assets or a Brent close above $118 opens new highs; a concrete US–Iran opening would take Brent toward $108.
oil.watch: Tehran talks, Saudi attacks, EIA data Oct 28, Dec Brent expiry Oct 30 and OPEC+ Nov 1.

gas.note: Nov RBOB rose 0.69¢ (+0.2%) to $3.2185, a fourth straight gain and the highest settle since Oct 16.
gas.why: Gasoline edged higher even as crude fell, widening its crack spread, as the thinly traded November contract heads into Friday's expiry. It has gained about 10¢ over four sessions, its best run since mid-September, though it is still down about 6% this month as cheaper winter-blend fuel and softer seasonal demand cap it. Diesel fell 1.5% to $4.91.
gas.outlook: Range $3.10–3.32 into expiry; December trades about 8¢ lower near $3.14, so the roll pulls the front-month quote down. A close above $3.30 would need Brent back above $118.
gas.watch: Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, EIA stocks Oct 28 and AAA's weekly pump average.

gold.note: Spot near $4,015, up about 0.5%, back above $4,000 after Friday's $3,975 low; resistance at $4,032 held.
gold.why: Gold recovered as a $2 drop in crude eased the inflation fears that drove last week's 4% slide, its worst since June, and bargain hunters treated $4,000 as support. The rebound stayed modest because futures still price 75–80% odds of a December Fed hike, the dollar is firm and Treasuries offering near 5% compete for haven money. Real 10-year yields have eased toward 2.6%, which limits the downside.
gold.outlook: Range $3,946–4,075 into the Fed. A statement that keeps December open would let it test $4,075; a clear hike signal plus a hot PCE on Oct 29 would break $3,946 and target $3,890.
gold.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, PCE and Q3 GDP Oct 29, and oil.

silver.note: Spot near $53.9, roughly flat; failed above $54.50 after a 6% weekly loss, gold/silver ratio near 74.
silver.why: Silver lagged gold's bounce, giving back an early rise to about $54.20 as growth worries after last week's AI-led equity selloff weighed on industrial metals. Lower oil helped only at the margin. Heraeus noted it has broken below its July lows and sits more than 20% under its August high near $70, though Fresnillo's 12% drop in third-quarter output is a reminder that mine supply is tightening.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $52.40–55.80 range. A break below $53.40 targets $52.40 and then $50; it needs a close above $55.80 to repair the trend.
silver.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, big-tech earnings, copper and China data.

us2y.note: Up about 3bp to near 4.71% after a soft $69bn auction stopped at 4.708%.
us2y.why: The 2-year edged higher as the $69bn auction tailed slightly, at 4.708% against 4.705% when-issued, and the market kept pricing a hold on Wednesday but 75–80% odds of a December hike. Lower oil took a little of the inflation edge off, which kept the move small. Deutsche Bank expects a hawkish message from Chair Warsh even with a pause.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.62–4.80%. A statement or press conference that signals December would lift it toward 4.80%; a clearly data-dependent tone or a soft PCE would pull it back to 4.62%.
us2y.watch: 5- and 7-year auctions, the Fed Oct 28, Q3 GDP and PCE Oct 29.

us5y.note: About 4.83%, up roughly 2bp with the front end before this week's 5-year sale.
us5y.why: The 5-year drifted higher with the 2-year as the soft 2-year auction and concession-building for the 5-year sale outweighed the drop in oil. Fed pricing barely moved, with markets treating this week as a pause in a hiking cycle rather than its end, and solid growth data keep the belly from rallying.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.74–4.95%. A hawkish Fed would push it toward 4.95%; a soft PCE or a renewed equity slide would retest 4.74%.
us5y.watch: The 5-year auction, the Fed Oct 28 and PCE Oct 29.

us10y.note: Near 4.99%, little changed; held just below 5% after Friday's 4bp rise.
us10y.why: The 10-year marked time ahead of the Fed and a heavy data week. Cheaper oil and lingering worries about debt-funded AI spending kept a lid on yields, while a firmer front end and Thursday's GDP and PCE kept buyers cautious. It remains well below the 5.365% 24-year high of Oct 7, and the curve flattened slightly as the 2-year rose.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.88–5.10%. Oil above $100 and heavy supply limit the downside; a hawkish Fed would put it back above 5%, while a soft PCE or a new tech selloff would test 4.88%.
us10y.watch: The Fed Oct 28, GDP and PCE Oct 29, the midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.

us30y.note: About 5.30%, down about 1bp; the curve flattened as the front end rose.
us30y.why: The long bond edged lower as lower oil trimmed inflation compensation and investors added to flatteners ahead of a Fed seen staying hawkish. Term-premium worries ahead of the midterms and the Nov 4 refunding kept the rally small.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.20–5.42%. Smaller long-bond auction sizes at the refunding would help it rally; unchanged sizes and oil back near $118 would push it toward 5.40%.
us30y.watch: The Fed Oct 28, the midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.

de2y.note: Near 3.08%, little changed; ECB hold priced for Thursday, hikes later.
de2y.why: The Schatz held steady as the Ifo index rose to 90.2, above the 90.0 forecast, offset by lower oil. Markets price about a 90% chance the ECB holds its 2.50% deposit rate on Thursday but expect a hike in coming months, with September inflation at 3.8%. Some see wider French spreads already tightening conditions enough to delay it.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.98–3.15%. A Lagarde signal for December would lift it toward 3.15%; concern about French spreads or weak inflation would test 2.98%.
de2y.watch: The ECB Oct 29 and flash October inflation at the end of the week.

de5y.note: About 3.17%, roughly flat as safe-haven demand eased.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund steadied as French relief drew money out of German debt while lower oil and a cautious ECB outlook held yields down. Ifo expectations rose to 91.6, the highest in over four years, but the current situation index fell to 88.8, showing energy and rates starting to weigh.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.08–3.25%. A hawkish ECB would push it to the top; renewed French stress would bring back the haven bid.
de5y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, euro-area inflation and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: About 3.36%, up about 1bp; spread to OATs narrowed about 13bp to near 154bp.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund rose slightly as Moody's decision to hold France at Aa3 reduced the haven demand that had kept German yields down last week. A sixth straight rise in Ifo to 90.2, beating forecasts, added a little pressure, while lower oil limited the rise. The spread to France fell from 167bp to around 154bp.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.28–3.45%. Further French relief and firm data tilt it higher; a dovish ECB or another oil spike that hits growth would cap it.
de10y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, euro inflation and French budget votes.

de30y.note: About 3.69%, little changed with the US long end.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund was steady as the slight fall in US long yields and cheaper oil offset reduced haven demand. It tracks global term premium and German fiscal expansion more than ECB pricing, so the quiet US long end kept it in range.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.80%. It follows US long bonds and German supply more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US long yields, the Nov 4 refunding and German long-dated sales.

fr2y.note: About 3.73%, down a few basis points after Moody's held France at Aa3.
fr2y.why: Short French debt joined the relief rally after Moody's kept its rating, though by less than longer maturities because the front end tracks ECB pricing. The agency's assumption that a deficit-cutting 2027 budget passes, possibly by decree, eased the near-term political tail risk, and weekend protests were calmer than the week before.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.65–3.82%. It stays anchored by the ECB unless the budget fails or a censure motion threatens the government.
fr2y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, French flash inflation and the budget debate.

fr5y.note: About 4.33%, down about 8–10bp as the OAT curve rallied.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT rallied after Moody's surprised with a hold, as investors who had positioned for a downgrade covered shorts. Commerzbank saw room for more rating relief, but Moody's still sees deficits of 5.4% of GDP this year and 5.2% next, above the 5% target, so buyers stayed selective.
fr5y.outlook: Bias lower in a 4.20–4.45% range. A budget setback in parliament or new unrest would send it back toward 4.45%.
fr5y.watch: The budget debate, the ECB Oct 29 and French inflation data.

fr10y.note: Down about 12bp to near 4.91%, below 5%; spread to Bunds down about 13bp to near 154bp.
fr10y.why: French 10-year yields fell sharply after Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, when many had expected a cut. The spread to Bunds posted its biggest one-day narrowing since 2020, from about 167bp to around 154bp, as Bund yields rose. Calmer weekend protests helped, but Moody's expects debt above 120% of GDP in 2027 and Barclays questioned how long the relief lasts.
fr10y.outlook: Spread bias narrower toward 145–150bp in a 145–170bp range. A failed budget vote or fresh unrest would put 167bp back in play.
fr10y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, budget votes in parliament and French inflation data.

fr30y.note: About 5.40%, down about 8–10bp, off its highs.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT eased with the rest of the curve after the Moody's hold, though less than the 10-year, as investors still want a large premium to hold long French debt through the budget fight and the 2027 presidential race. Debt above 120% of GDP keeps the long end the most exposed point on the curve.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.30–5.55%. A credible budget deal would extend the rally; a close above 5.55% would signal the relief has run out.
fr30y.watch: The budget debate, long-dated OAT auctions and the ECB Oct 29.

watch: Next: the Fed decision Oct 28 with EIA stocks the same day, the ECB, US Q3 GDP and PCE on Oct 29, Nov RBOB and Dec Brent expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ on Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.
sources: Dow Jones via MarketScreener (Treasuries, Bunds, OATs)
